messages.text: I have a green card, got it 2 years ago. My kids were born here. Can my family get food stamps or Medicaid?

Thanks for telling me. I can check this with you. A caseworker or a legal aid group can confirm how your immigration status applies. Your kids were born here, so they are U.S. citizens, and children who are citizens can often get help even when a parent's status is complicated.

Two questions to start:

1. Who lives with you and shares food? Please give each person's age. Tell me if anyone is pregnant or has a disability.
2. What income does each adult get before taxes, and how often are they paid (weekly, every two weeks, or monthly)?
Just me and my two kids, ages 6 and 3. Nobody's pregnant or disabled. I make $1,800 a month before taxes, paid monthly.

Yes, your family may be able to get help. Your kids look like the strongest cases.

**Health coverage (TennCare/CoverKids): likely for your kids**
- Your 6-year-old and 3-year-old look likely to qualify. Your income of $1,800 a month is under the limits for a family of 3. The limit is $3,028 for age 6 and $3,233 for age 3.
- For you, a caseworker needs to look at it. Adult coverage depends on immigration status.
- Apply at TennCare Connect: https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov/ or call 855-259-0701.
- Sources: [TennCare Eligibility Reference Guide](https://www.tn.gov/coverkids/coverkids/redirect-income-guidelines.html) and [42 CFR 435.406](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/section-435.406).

**WIC: likely for your 3-year-old**
- WIC serves children under 5. Your income is under the limit of $4,212 a month for 3 people.
- Immigration status doesn't affect WIC in Tennessee.
- The clinic will do a short health and nutrition check.
- Apply at a local health department clinic: https://www.tn.gov/health/wic.html or call 1-800-342-5942.
- Source: [USDA WIC income guidelines, 2026-27](https://www.fns.usda.gov/wic/fr-042926).

**Food assistance (SNAP): a caseworker needs to look at this**
- Rules for non-citizens changed in 2025 and depend on your immigration status, so a caseworker has to check yours. Your U.S.-born kids can still get SNAP.
- If only the income is counted, the screening shows about **$441 a month**. This is only an estimate. It may change if your status affects the amount.
- Apply at https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp?id=start_snap_application or call 866-311-4287.
- Sources: [USDA SNAP eligibility](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/recipient/eligibility) and [USDA 2027 SNAP limits](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/allotment/cola).

**Two things to know**
- I didn't know your age, so I entered 30 as a placeholder. If you tell me your real age, I can rerun the screening.
- I haven't counted rent, utilities, or child care yet. Those could raise your SNAP amount.

**Questions for you**
1. How much is your rent or mortgage? Do you pay separately for heating or cooling, other utilities, or none?
2. Do you pay for child care so you can work? If so, how much each month?

You can also dial 211 for free help applying.

This is a screening, not a decision. Only the state agency decides, and you can apply for anything even if the screening looks unsure. For help with how your green card affects your case, a caseworker or a legal aid group can check.
rent is $850. heating and cooling are separate, we pay for those. no other utilities. no child care, the kids are at school and our neighbor watches them. oh and i'm 32, not 30 like you put down.

Thanks for the details and for correcting your age. Your rent and heating and cooling costs raised the SNAP estimate. The answers for the other programs didn't change.

**Food assistance (SNAP): a caseworker needs to look at this**
- Without the immigration question, the screening shows about **$658 a month**. That's up from $441 because your rent and utilities lower the income SNAP counts. It is only an estimate.
- The immigration question still needs a caseworker. Non-citizen rules changed in 2025 and depend on your status. Your U.S.-born kids can still get SNAP.
- Your income is under the limits for a family of 3. The gross limit is $2,960 and the net limit is $2,277.
- One caution: the utility figure I used is the latest published one, which was in effect only until 9/30/2026. Newer numbers weren't available, so the final amount could differ.
- Savings: the federal limit is $3,000 in cash and bank accounts. I didn't ask about yours, so this isn't counted yet.
- Apply: https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp?id=start_snap_application or 866-311-4287.
- Sources: [USDA 2027 SNAP limits](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/allotment/cola), [USDA SNAP eligibility](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/recipient/eligibility), and [USDA utility allowances](https://www.fns.usda.gov/sites/default/files/resource-files/2026-05-21-SUA-Table-FY26.xlsx).

**TennCare/CoverKids: likely for both kids**
- Your income of $1,800 is under the limits of $3,028 for your 6-year-old and $3,233 for your 3-year-old.
- For you, TennCare Connect or a caseworker needs to check, because adult coverage depends on immigration status.
- Apply: https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov/ or 855-259-0701.
- Source: [TennCare Eligibility Reference Guide](https://www.tn.gov/coverkids/coverkids/redirect-income-guidelines.html).

**WIC: likely for your 3-year-old**
- Your income is under the limit of $4,212 a month. Your immigration status doesn't affect WIC in Tennessee. There is a short health check at the clinic.
- Apply at a local health department clinic: https://www.tn.gov/health/wic.html or 1-800-342-5942.
- Source: [USDA WIC income guidelines](https://www.fns.usda.gov/wic/fr-042926).

**What to do next**
1. Apply for all three. You can apply even if you're unsure.
2. Report your income, household, and status accurately on each application. That protects you, because benefits paid by mistake have to be paid back.
3. For help with the immigration questions, call 211 or ask a legal aid group.

Do you or the kids already get SNAP, WIC, or TennCare? If so, tell me and I'll adjust. Also, about how much do you have in cash and bank accounts? You don't have to say.

This is a screening, not a decision. Only the state agency decides who qualifies.
no, we don't get any of those right now. and we have about $200 in savings.

Thanks. Your $200 in savings is well under the $3,000 federal limit for cash and bank accounts, so it won't get in the way. The results are the same, and I have everything I need.

**Where you stand**
- **TennCare/CoverKids: likely for both kids.** Your income of $1,800 is under the limits ($3,028 for your 6-year-old, $3,233 for your 3-year-old). For you, a caseworker needs to check, because adult coverage depends on immigration status. Source: [TennCare Eligibility Reference Guide](https://www.tn.gov/coverkids/coverkids/redirect-income-guidelines.html).
- **WIC: likely for your 3-year-old.** Your income is under the $4,212 limit, and your immigration status doesn't affect WIC in Tennessee. There is a short health check at the clinic. Source: [USDA WIC guidelines](https://www.fns.usda.gov/wic/fr-042926).
- **Food assistance (SNAP): a caseworker needs to look at this.** Without the immigration question, the estimate is about **$658 a month**. It is only an estimate. Your U.S.-born kids can still get SNAP. Sources: [USDA SNAP limits](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/allotment/cola) and [USDA SNAP eligibility](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/recipient/eligibility).
- The utility figure behind the SNAP estimate was in effect only until 9/30/2026. Newer numbers weren't available, so the final amount could differ.

**Where to apply**
1. **TennCare/CoverKids:** https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov/ or 855-259-0701
2. **WIC:** a local health department clinic (https://www.tn.gov/health/wic.html) or 1-800-342-5942
3. **SNAP:** https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp?id=start_snap_application or 866-311-4287
4. **Free local help:** dial 211

When you apply, list everyone in your home and your income exactly as it is. That protects you, because benefits paid by mistake have to be paid back. A caseworker or a legal aid group can answer questions about how your green card affects your case.

This is a screening, not a decision. Only the state agency decides who qualifies, and you can apply for any of these even if you're unsure.
